findings.message: The plan designs journal.py around ONE emit() choke point with 'monotonic per-project seq assignment, atomic append under WRITE_LOCK' — a single-process design (WRITE_LOCK is a process-local lock) — and then Phase 6 moves job ownership into a SECOND process while 'job launched/finished/cancelled' remains on the C3 mandatory event list. The plan never says who emits job-lifecycle events after the split. Every option breaks something unaddressed: (a) the supervisor appends to the same per-project JSONL → two writers, seq monotonicity and the lock are void, and the distro-style 'no writes outside the module' scan is violated by construction; (b) the dashboard emits on the supervisor's behalf → job-finished events that occur while the dashboard is restarting (the EXACT scenario C4 exists to survive) are dropped or need an unplanned replay-on-reconnect protocol; (c) supervisor-local journal segments → an unplanned merge/ordering design. Phase 6 even claims it 'benefits from the journal (durable job records) already being in place' — asserting the interaction is a benefit while its core design hole (D1×D2 composition) is nowhere in the plan. This must be a designed row in the Stage-2 IPC contract table, not discovered mid-EXECUTE.

The gate claims to render the OLD f-string path and the NEW static+bootstrap path and diff 'byte-for-byte after {{/}} de-escaping'. That is definitionally unachievable for increment (3), the generate_html f-string — the one the plan itself calls 'the only genuinely fiddly one'. The old path emits JS with server data VALUES baked into the code text; the new path emits static JS that READS those values from ANCHOR_BOOT. Wherever a data interpolation existed, the bytes MUST differ — that is the entire point of the extraction. So byte-parity holds only for the interpolation-free blobs (_PROJECT_WINDOW_JS, the shell), i.e. exactly where the risk isn't, and silently degrades to nothing on the increment where the risk lives. The plan needs an honest gate for increment 3: e.g. a fixed-fixture render (pin the data, compare the old baked output against new-static-plus-boot-JSON evaluated over the same fixture) or a token-level diff that treats each censused interpolation site as an expected delta. As written, the plan's 'safest big diff' claim rests on a gate that cannot run where it matters.

The census bullet pre-commits to amending the LOCKED C1 bar 'if markup-emitting interpolations exceed a small threshold' — but 'a small threshold' is never defined (5? 50? 500?), so the trigger for weakening a locked success criterion is left to mid-effort discretion, which is precisely what a locked North Star exists to prevent. The drift rule says amendments go through the documented path with John's approval; the plan should state the numeric threshold NOW (so the census output mechanically decides), state what the amended bar would concretely be, and state explicitly that crossing the threshold produces an amendment PROPOSAL to John, not an automatic re-bar. As written, this is an escape hatch sized to fit whatever the census finds.

The tripwire wraps 'file writes under .anchor/' and is then promoted to THE mechanical enumeration of the mutation-of-record set and the permanent C3 completeness gate. But C3's own event list includes mutations that do NOT write under .anchor/: 'doc persisted' (persist_session_docs copies docs into the main project folder and git-commits them), project lifecycle actions touching per-project folders, and the global rnd_jobs/ store (repo-root, not per-project .anchor/). Task-markdown mutations are arguably out (markdown stays source of truth), but doc-persistence is explicitly IN the C3 list and outside the tripwire's watch. The Phase-5 instrumentation is 'designed against evidence' from a sensor that is blind to part of the required set — the enumeration will be mechanically complete about the wrong universe. The tripwire scope must be derived FROM the C3 event list (all durable-store write sites, wherever they live), not from one directory prefix; and it must survive the Phase-4 ANCHOR_DATA_DIR move that relocates the very paths it keys on.

The parity gate classifies 'journal-ahead=OK/crash-residue' with no stated bound other than the tail window's recency tolerance. Combined with journal-first-by-decree, this makes the single most likely dual-write failure mode — the legacy-store write silently failing or being skipped after emit() (a bug, not a crash) — indistinguishable from benign crash residue. A persistent legacy-write regression would produce a steadily growing journal-ahead population that the gate waves through forever, and C3's 'zero divergence' claim quietly becomes 'zero divergence of the classes we chose to count'. The classification needs teeth: journal-ahead events OLDER than the bounded tail window (or exceeding a count threshold, or recurring for the same event type across runs) must classify as BUG, and the reconcile-report must surface the journal-ahead census so a trend is visible. Otherwise the gate proves less than the criterion states.

findings.section: Phase 5 — envelope design vs parity/rebuild deliverables
findings.message: The envelope is 'validated against the three Phase-0 Butler user stories, answerable from envelope fields alone' — but C3's actual proof obligations are different and strictly harder: the parity gate must RE-DERIVE session/effort views from the journal, and rebuild_index.py must reconstruct a deleted index.json. Answering 'what happened on project X this week' requires correlation/actor/ts; rebuilding an index row requires every field the legacy record carries (labels, lanes, chain_id, parent ids, doc rels, statuses, provenance…). The plan validates the schema against the easy consumer and merely asserts the hard consumers will work. There is no payload-completeness gate — no rule that each event type's payload must be sufficient to reconstruct the legacy-store delta it shadows, checked mechanically (e.g. the rebuild test failing on ANY missing field, run per event type, not once against a happy-path fixture). Without it, the schema will be discovered insufficient at rebuild time, forcing either payload-widening churn (schema ver bump per discovery) or a rebuild tool that quietly consults the legacy stores it is supposed to reconstruct.

C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms 'dispatch through a single declarative table'. The draft's phase gate is explicitly weaker — 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms' — and closure permits the residual to be 'explicitly carried as named debt'. Two problems. First, a route with a declared ROW that still DISPATCHES via the legacy if-elif chain does not satisfy 'dispatch through a single table', and worse, the draft's own strangler wording ('table first, UNMATCHED falls through to the legacy chains') implies an unmigrated route's declared auth policy is never actually EXECUTED on its request path — the row is documentation, not enforcement, for the entire migration tail. Second, the North Star sanctions exactly two narrowings (PTY spike 'no', John declining tokened ops); 'legacy arms carried as named debt' is a third, unsanctioned one smuggled in via the closure phase. Either the plan commits to zero legacy arms within the effort as a C2-blocking gate, or it must route the residual through the amendment path — the scorecard cannot mark C2 met/narrowed on 'named debt'.

Phase 0 declares 'Nothing here changes runtime behavior' and defers 'any product-behavior change', yet one of its bullets SHIPS a frontend↔backend protocol change: ANCHOR_BOOT carrying a build id, every _postJson sending it, a new structured 409 path, and a reload-required banner. That is product behavior deployed to the live service — a direct internal contradiction with the phase's C7-risk-near-zero framing. It also has an ordering problem: ANCHOR_BOOT is defined in Phase 1 (extraction) as the bootstrap channel the extraction CREATES; in Phase 0 the frontend is still the embedded f-string, so the shim must be retrofitted into the blob that is about to be verbatim-moved — meaning the 'verbatim move' baseline and the Phase-0 census both shift AFTER the census runs. Sequence it honestly: either the shim is a named exception to Phase 0's no-behavior-change rule with its own smoke gate and the census re-run after it lands, or it becomes increment 0 of the extraction phase.

The same phase requires the static-vs-embedded off-switch flag to stay 'functional through the phase' AND an exit gate of ≥7,000 lines shrunk. These are mutually exclusive at any single commit: if the embedded f-string path is retained so the flag can flip back, anchor_gui.py has not shrunk; if the blob is deleted to achieve the shrink, the flag's 'embedded' position is dead code-paths pointing at nothing. The overview's blanket claim that 'each merged wave [is] revertible without reverting later waves via per-pillar off-switch flags' is therefore false for this pillar the moment the shrink gate passes — frontend revert becomes git-revert, which later phases touching anchor_gui.py will conflict with. State the actual mechanism per increment: flag-coexistence during the increment's soak, then blob deletion as its own commit, after which revert is git-level and time-bounded.

The two cited blobs total ~7,367 lines (4,663 + 2,706) — only ~5% over the 7,000 bar — and the extraction ADDS code to anchor_gui.py (bootstrap-JSON builder, static-root route wiring, build-id minting, cache-bust hashing). If 'shrinks by ≥7,000 lines' is measured as net file-length delta (the natural reading), a few hundred lines of new seam code eat the entire margin and the criterion fails on arithmetic while the work succeeds on substance. The plan should define the measurement now (net wc -l delta of anchor_gui.py, before-vs-after the phase) and let the Phase-0 census confirm the margin, rather than discovering the definition fight at the exit gate.

A 'soak day' per route batch on a single-user service exercises John's daily flows and one 5AM healthcheck run, but the consumer inventory the plan itself commissions includes weekly-or-rarer callers: weekly-review habits, occasional .bat/.vbs launcher paths, the iPad PWA over Tailscale (used intermittently), and scheduled tasks that don't fire daily. A warn window that is shorter than the slowest consumer's cadence cannot produce the evidence the gate claims. Either the warn log review must be cross-checked against the Phase-0 consumer inventory as a CHECKLIST (every enumerated consumer observed, or affirmatively exercised by hand) rather than time-boxed, or the soak must span the slowest known cadence for the routes in the batch.

The migration script sets the env for the NSSM anchor service, but the runtime-state seam is read by MORE entry points: the 'Anchor Health Check' scheduled task (5AM, own environment), 'Anchor Healthcheck.bat', the new supervisor service (Phase 6 clones AppEnvironmentExtra — good, but that's two phases later), and any ad-hoc `python anchor.py rnd …` shell John or a session opens in the repo. Any entry point missing the env silently falls back to the repo-local default and either re-litters the repo (breaking C6's 'stays clean') or, worse, reads a stale split-brain copy of the registry/journal while the service writes the relocated one. The plan needs an explicit propagation checklist (machine-level env var, or every launcher/task rewritten) plus a paths.py-level tripwire that logs/refuses when the resolved data dir is under the repo root post-migration — otherwise 'stays clean through a healthcheck cycle' proves only the one entry point that was scripted.

Probe (b) restarts the SUPERVISOR service nightly/daily from the healthcheck, but service restart on Windows requires elevation and the 5AM healthcheck runs as a non-elevated scheduled task under .\john (the same reason the existing docs say `nssm restart anchor` needs an elevated shell). Either the probe silently degrades to never running (and C4's continuous proof evaporates into the one-time runbook), or the healthcheck task gets elevated rights (a security posture change nobody reviewed), or the supervisor needs a token-authed self-restart IPC verb (new attack surface). The plan should pick one now — this is exactly the kind of 'gate that can't actually run in its scheduled context' the Phase-0 SLO discipline exists to catch, and it's sitting inside the plan's own bullet.

The ConPTY-across-processes spike runs in Phase 0 but is consumed five phases later, after the extraction, route migration, data-dir move, and journal have all reshaped the codebase (and possibly terminal_session's surroundings). A months-old spike verdict — especially a 'yes' with a latency/complexity budget measured against the pre-refactor code — may no longer describe the system Phase 6 builds on. The plan should either time-bound the verdict's validity (re-affirm the spike's acceptance answers against the then-current code before Phase-6 EXECUTE) or state why the spike's findings are architecture-invariant (pure OS-level ConPTY handle semantics, independent of Anchor's code shape). Cheap to add; prevents building the PTY decision on expired evidence.

Both Phase 0 and Phase 7 lean on 'each new walk runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run', but no nightly repetition harness exists today and no phase's near-term specifics builds one — it appears only as a ritual to 'codify'. 20 nightly runs of four new walks is a real scheduled-task + report-aggregation + flake-classification deliverable, and it sits on the critical path of every pillar's healthcheck promotion. Name it as a Phase-0 build item with an owner phase, or the SLO discipline becomes a rule everyone agrees with and nobody can execute.

Every heading carries two colliding indices ('Phase 1 — Phase 0 — Ground Truth…', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — Event-Log Spine'), and the overview's DAG uses yet a third naming (P0/C1/C2…). Foreman waves, gate artifacts, and John's approvals will reference 'Phase 4' and mean two different things. Pick one index before Stage 2 — off-by-one ambiguity in a plan whose whole pitch is mechanical unambiguity.

The overview claims 'All 52 integrated ideas are absorbed' but the draft ships no traceability table, so the claim is unverifiable by exactly the standard the plan preaches (demonstrated, not narrated). A reviewer cannot confirm from the scattered '(Integrated N)' citations that all of 1–52 appear or that none was silently dropped. Attach the 52-row idea→phase map as a plan appendix. (Process hygiene, not a North-Star criterion — flagged at honest severity.)

Every phase carries TWO numbers ('Phase 1 — Phase 0', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — Event-Log Spine') and body text cross-references use the inner scheme ('the Phase-3 event envelope' means the header-Phase-5 journal; 'Phase-4 sequencing' means the header-Phase-6 supervisor). Two live numbering schemes in a document that Stage 2 and Foreman will consume mechanically is a misrouting defect, not cosmetics: a wave sequenced against the wrong 'Phase 3' violates the dependency DAG the plan itself declares (journal after data-dir move, supervisor after spike verdict). Collapse to one numbering scheme before Stage 2 or this WILL produce a sequencing error.

findings.section: Phase 0 near-term specifics (contract-versioning shim) vs its own deferrals
findings.message: Phase 0's deferral list says 'Any product-behavior change — Phase 0 is instrumentation, spikes, and process artifacts only', yet the same phase ships the frontend↔backend contract shim LIVE ('in the LAST pre-migration release'): new client header on every _postJson, new server 409 path, new banner UI. That is a deployed product-behavior change by any definition. Worse, the shim is specified as 'ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id' — but window.ANCHOR_BOOT is created by the extraction phase that runs AFTER Phase 0; pre-extraction there is no bootstrap JSON for the build id to ride in, so the shim as written depends on an artifact from its own future. Either the shim gets its own pre-extraction injection mechanism (spelled out), or it moves into extraction increment 1 — as drafted the plan's very first deliverable is unimplementable as specified and contradicts its own phase contract.

The gate claims OLD-f-string vs NEW-static output is diffed 'byte-for-byte after {{/}} de-escaping', with Playwright reserved for the bootstrap seam. But increment 3 — the generate_html f-string JS/CSS — contains DATA interpolations by construction (the entire reason the Phase-0 census exists). Post-extraction, every data interpolation becomes an ANCHOR_BOOT read or API call, so the static file is NOT byte-equal to the rendered old output precisely in the regions where the risk lives. Byte-parity is only honest for interpolation-free spans. As written, the plan's central C1 gate cannot go green for the one increment it calls 'the only genuinely fiddly one', which means it will be quietly weakened mid-wave — the exact failure mode Phase 0 exists to prevent. Specify the real comparison now: render BOTH paths against one pinned state and compare post-substitution output, or byte-compare only census-classified static spans with the interpolated spans enumerated and Playwright-covered individually.

C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms 'dispatch through a single declarative table'. Phase 2's gate is explicitly weakened to 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms', and closure then offers 'driven to zero OR its residual explicitly carried as named debt'. 'Named debt' is a narrowing channel that bypasses the North Star's amendment rule — the scorecard clause says any narrowing goes through the documented amendment path, yet this sentence pre-authorizes shipping C2 unmet as mere debt. A competitor plan would be pinned to the criterion: either the zero-arm milestone is a binding exit condition of the effort (state which phase owns it), or the residual case is routed through a John-approved amendment, never a debt register.

findings.section: Phase 0 smoke ritual + Phase 5 drain fallback
findings.message: The per-wave smoke ritual restarts the anchor service at EVERY merged increment across all seven phases, and until the supervisor phase lands, restarts kill in-flight jobs and live PTY sessions — John's actual daily use. The plan pre-DESIGNS the graceful drain (park + capture_session_docs + warm-resume seed) in Phase 0 but only SHIPS it in Phase 5/6 'in the same wave as any narrowing'. That leaves the entire extraction, route, hygiene, and journal campaign — the bulk of the effort's deploys — destroying live context on every merge, which strains 'John's daily use never breaks' for months while the fix sits designed-but-unshipped. Ship the drain script as a Phase-0 deliverable (it composes existing, already-tested primitives: close_session, capture_session_docs, W3 resume) and make it part of the smoke ritual from wave one.

C3's bar is 'reports zero divergence'. The gate as designed tolerates a bounded tail window and classifies journal-ahead as OK/crash-residue. Engineering-wise this is defensible, but it is not the locked criterion — it is a redefinition embedded inside a gate implementation. State the delta explicitly (zero divergence AFTER quiescence and journal-ahead reconciliation, with journal-ahead bounded and replayed) and, if that is a narrowing, route it through the amendment path rather than shipping a gate that reports green against a softer bar than the one John locked.

The de-fork gate is 'today's REAL markdown files parsed identically pre/post'. If those files (domains/commercial.md carries proprietary fundraising and relationship detail) are snapshotted into a committed test corpus, the repo's own no-PII/secrets discipline (distro.py scan) is violated and sensitive data gets frozen into git history. Specify now: the golden run executes against the live files in place (uncommitted, environment-local) or against a synthetic corpus that covers every parse construct; a committed real-data corpus is not an option.

'Warn for a soak day' assumes consumers fire daily. This system's callers are cadence-driven: the 5AM healthcheck fires once a day, scheduled tasks and launchers fire irregularly, and the iPad PWA may not be opened for days. A 24-hour warn window can therefore certify a route batch clean while a weekly or occasional consumer is about to be locked out. Bind the soak to coverage, not time: at least one full healthcheck cycle PLUS an affirmative check that every consumer the Phase-0 enumeration listed for those routes appeared in the warn log (or was manually exercised) before enforce.

'Loopback token-authed IPC' is asserted but never specified: same ANCHOR_TOKEN or a distinct supervisor token; whether the supervisor's HTTP surface gets the same default-deny declarative route treatment the effort just built for the dashboard (a second hand-rolled if-elif server would recreate the C2 disease in a new process); and how the token stays in sync across two NSSM services' AppEnvironmentExtra when rotated. install_supervisor.ps1 'clones' the env once — rotation drift between the two services is an unhandled failure row that belongs in the IPC contract table.

Each of the four new walks must run '20× nightly' before joining the 5AM run, but no nightly-repetition mechanism exists or is planned — that is a new scheduled task (an ops-surface addition the non-goals say this effort doesn't make beyond the supervisor service) and, read literally, ~20 nights of serialized calendar time per walk at the very end of the effort. Define the mechanism now and allow accelerated repetition (20 consecutive runs in one night satisfies the same flake-detection intent) so closure isn't a multi-week idle soak.

'Old dir preserved read-only for a week' is a backup, not a rollback plan. Any rollback invoked after real use resumes on the new dir silently discards the sessions, efforts, and (later) journals written there in the interim. Specify the actual rollback procedure — reverse-migrate new-dir deltas back, or an explicit accept-loss statement with the window bounded — so the 'rollback-able unit' claim is honest rather than nominal.

The census step says if markup-emitting interpolations exceed a threshold, 'amend the North-Star C1 bar ... NOW'. Amendments require John's decision; the plan phrases this as an automatic consequence of a script's output. Rephrase as a decision gate: census output → present the evidence and the amendment option to John → proceed on his answer. Also state the threshold numerically before the census runs, or the 'small threshold' becomes negotiable after the fact.

A competing plan would carry rough per-phase wave counts and calendar expectations so the seven-phase sequence (with two spikes, a merge freeze, and a 20-night soak) can be sanity-checked against John's tolerance for a months-long substrate effort. No North-Star criterion demands estimates, so this is demoted — but Stage 2 should surface it.

C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms route through the single declarative table. The draft quietly redefines the phase gate as 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms', and Phase 7 permits closure with the remaining-legacy-arms counter 'driven to zero OR its residual explicitly carried as named debt'. 'Named debt' is not the documented North-Star amendment path — it is a unilateral criterion dilution pre-authorized inside the plan. A route with a table ROW whose bytes still execute through the legacy if-elif chain has not migrated; the in-branch import-shadowing class C2 also demands dead ('zero remain') survives in every unmigrated arm. Either commit to zero legacy arms as a hard C2 exit condition of the effort, or route the narrowing through the amendment path with John's approval NOW — the plan may not ship its own loophole.

The bored-investor problem: Stage-0's own oranges framing ranks the event log as the highest-Butler-value pillar and names the supervisor split as the fix for John's REAL recurring pain (nssm restart kills in-flight Foreman runs), yet the plan lands them 5th and 6th of 7 phases, behind frontend extraction, route migration, and repo hygiene. If the effort stalls at 50% — the base case for multi-month re-architectures — John holds a smaller file and identical pain. The dependencies asserted to justify this are thin or fabricated: the journal instruments effort_history/session_registry/terminal_session/job_runner, none of which is blocked by the anchor_gui frontend blobs or the route table; the jobs-half supervisor is called 'low-risk, immediately delivers restart survival' by Stage-0 D2 itself and needs neither the journal (job_runner already has durable records + job-object + creation-time identity) nor 'IPC-adjacent auth' from the route table (loopback token IPC reuses paths.auth_ok directly). Only the data-dir move (journals born outside the repo) is a real ordering constraint. Re-sequence so at least one of C3/C4 (recommend the jobs-half supervisor) lands in the first half of the effort, or state honestly why value is being deferred.

Phase 0 defers to build-time ground truth that is cheap, mechanical, and knowable during planning — and whose answer gates the plan's own validity. The interpolation census in particular decides whether the C1 bar (≥7,000-line shrink, ~50-line blob cap) must be amended 'NOW, not mid-wave' — meaning the plan is being locked while explicitly anticipating an immediate amendment to its first success criterion. A grep-classifiable census over two known line ranges, the consumer-enumeration grep, the dependency DAG, and the three Butler user stories are all Stage-1/Stage-2 planning artifacts; running them DURING Stage 2 (before Foreman) resolves the C1 bar, the open-route consumer set, and the event-envelope validation target before anything is committed. As drafted, Phase 0 is ~12 deliverables spanning two spikes, a Playwright suite, a tripwire harness, a deploy shim, process rituals, and a freeze protocol — a whole sub-project labeled 'instrumentation' with no sizing, delaying all user-visible value behind it. Pull the paper artifacts into Stage 2; keep Phase 0 to the two spikes, the Playwright flows, and the tripwire.

The plan decrees emit-event-THEN-write-legacy at every mutation-of-record, but never specifies what happens when emit() itself FAILS (disk full, schema-validation bug, lock contention, a malformed payload from one of ~10 instrumented subsystems). If emit() raising blocks the legacy write, a journal bug takes down the authoritative store path across session lifecycle, jobs, grass, and deliverables simultaneously — inverting D1 ('legacy stores stay authoritative') and violating C7, with the blast radius of the one choke point the design celebrates. The off-switch flag is a human-latency remedy, not a failure semantic. The plan must state the rule: emit() is fail-open with respect to the legacy write (log + counter + healthcheck surface on journal-write failure; legacy write ALWAYS proceeds), and the parity gate's classification must include 'legacy-ahead-because-emit-failed' as distinguishable from the BUG class.

Seven phases, roughly sixty near-term specifics, two spikes, four new healthcheck walks, a second NSSM service — and not one phase carries a size, wave count, or rough duration. The investor cannot judge whether the Phase-0 front-load pays back, whether the extraction merge-freeze window is days or weeks (it must be coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build, which needs a real window, not 'a soft freeze'), or whether the plan fits any horizon at all. C7's no-multi-day-freeze and never-broken-increment clauses are unverifiable without at least coarse per-phase sizing and an explicit statement of what gets CUT first if the effort must shrink. A FULL-pipeline Stage-1 master plan should rank the phases by value-per-cost and mark the minimum shippable subset (per the North Star: jobs-half C4 is non-negotiable; C1's bar is amendable) — this draft treats all seven phases as equally mandatory and unpriced.

Phase 0's framing paragraph claims 'Nothing here changes runtime behavior, so C7 risk is near zero', yet one of its own deliverables ships a frontend↔backend contract shim to the LIVE service: ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, the server 409s a mismatch. That is a client+server behavior change with its own stale-tab failure modes — exactly the class it exists to prevent. Worse, window.ANCHOR_BOOT does not exist until the Phase-1 extraction introduces the bootstrap JSON; in Phase 0 the build id must ride the still-embedded f-string, meaning the shim is built twice or the plan's dependency arrow is backwards. State honestly that Phase 0 contains one behavior-bearing deploy, and specify the pre-extraction carrier for the build id.

findings.section: Phase 1 (Phase 0) write-site tripwire / Phase 5 completeness gate
findings.message: Phase 0 says the tripwire 'fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event' and 'stays on forever' — but no journal exists until Phase 5, so between Phase 0 and Phase 5 the tripwire in failing mode would redden the entire suite. It plainly needs two modes (enumerate/report in Phases 0–4, enforce from Phase 5), yet the plan never says so, nor who owns the allowlist of legitimately-unjournaled writes (per-tick/telemetry 'excluded BY RULE' — which rule, checked where?) as the codebase drifts between the two phases. Specify the mode switch, its flip point, and the allowlist's review discipline, or the C3 completeness gate is a gate only in narrative.

C3 requires the parity gate to report ZERO divergence; the draft's gate 'tolerates a bounded tail window of recent events' and classifies journal-ahead as OK. Reasonable engineering for a live 5AM run, but as written it is a weaker predicate than the criterion. Make the two-tier structure explicit: the TEST-suite parity gate runs quiescent and asserts literal zero divergence (the C3 bar), while the live healthcheck run applies the bounded-tail classification with journal-ahead-within-window as the only tolerated class — and any legacy-ahead or conflict is a hard failure in both tiers. Otherwise the scorecard will mark C3 'met' against a diluted definition.

The plan repeatedly invokes a rule that each new healthcheck walk 'runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run', but the host has exactly one scheduled run (5AM) — there is no nightly-repetition harness, no scheduled task for it, and no phase deliverable that builds one. Four new walks (journal parity, supervisor probes, cookie/auth, relocated-data-dir) are gated on this nonexistent infrastructure. Either name the harness as a Phase-0/Phase-6 deliverable (a second scheduled task + a repetition report) or replace the rule with something the current infrastructure can enforce.

The preamble asserts 'All 52 integrated ideas are absorbed' and specifics cite opaque tags (Integrated 1..52, Mitigation 1..20) that appear nowhere in the North Star or the visible research input, so neither the Sharks nor the Judge can verify absorption or spot a silently dropped idea. Attach the numbered idea/mitigation ledger as a plan appendix or drop the claim.

findings.message: The plan designs journal.py around ONE emit() choke point with 'monotonic per-project seq assignment, atomic append under WRITE_LOCK' — a single-process design (WRITE_LOCK is a process-local lock) — and then Phase 6 moves job ownership into a SECOND process while 'job launched/finished/cancelled' remains on the C3 mandatory event list. The plan never says who emits job-lifecycle events after the split. Every option breaks something unaddressed: (a) the supervisor appends to the same per-project JSONL → two writers, seq monotonicity and the lock are void, and the distro-style 'no writes outside the module' scan is violated by construction; (b) the dashboard emits on the supervisor's behalf → job-finished events that occur while the dashboard is restarting (the EXACT scenario C4 exists to survive) are dropped or need an unplanned replay-on-reconnect protocol; (c) supervisor-local journal segments → an unplanned merge/ordering design. findings.message: The gate claims to render the OLD f-string path and the NEW static+bootstrap path and diff 'byte-for-byte after {{/}} de-escaping'. That is definitionally unachievable for increment (3), the generate_html f-string — the one the plan itself calls 'the only genuinely fiddly one'. The old path emits JS with server data VALUES baked into the code text; the new path emits static JS that READS those values from ANCHOR_BOOT. Wherever a data interpolation existed, the bytes MUST differ — that is the entire point of the extraction. So byte-parity holds only for the interpolation-free blobs (_PROJECT_WINDOW_JS, the shell), i.e. exactly where the risk isn't, and silently degrades to nothing on the increment where the risk lives. The plan needs an honest gate for increment 3: e.g. a fixed-fixture render (pin the data, compare the old baked output against new-static-plus-boot-JSON evaluated over the same fixture) or a token-level diff that treats each censused interpolation site as an expected delta. As written, the plan's 'safest big diff' claim rests on a gate that cannot run where it matters.

findings.topic: pre-authorized C1 amendment with undefined threshold
findings.message: The census bullet pre-commits to amending the LOCKED C1 bar 'if markup-emitting interpolations exceed a small threshold' — but 'a small threshold' is never defined (5? 50? 500?), so the trigger for weakening a locked success criterion is left to mid-effort discretion, which is precisely what a locked North Star exists to prevent. The drift rule says amendments go through the documented path with John's approval; the plan should state the numeric threshold NOW (so the census output mechanically decides), state what the amended bar would concretely be, and state explicitly that crossing the threshold produces an amendment PROPOSAL to John, not an automatic re-bar. As written, this is an escape hatch sized to fit whatever the census finds.

findings.topic: tripwire scope misses mutations outside .anchor/
findings.message: The tripwire wraps 'file writes under .anchor/' and is then promoted to THE mechanical enumeration of the mutation-of-record set and the permanent C3 completeness gate. But C3's own event list includes mutations that do NOT write under .anchor/: 'doc persisted' (persist_session_docs copies docs into the main project folder and git-commits them), project lifecycle actions touching per-project folders, and the global rnd_jobs/ store (repo-root, not per-project .anchor/). Task-markdown mutations are arguably out (markdown stays source of truth), but doc-persistence is explicitly IN the C3 list and outside the tripwire's watch. The Phase-5 instrumentation is 'designed against evidence' from a sensor that is blind to part of the required set — the enumeration will be mechanically complete about the wrong universe. The tripwire scope must be derived FROM the C3 event list (all durable-store write sites, wherever they live), not from one directory prefix; and it must survive the Phase-4 ANCHOR_DATA_DIR move that relocates the very paths it keys on.

findings.topic: journal-ahead classified OK masks dropped legacy writes
findings.message: The parity gate classifies 'journal-ahead=OK/crash-residue' with no stated bound other than the tail window's recency tolerance. Combined with journal-first-by-decree, this makes the single most likely dual-write failure mode — the legacy-store write silently failing or being skipped after emit() (a bug, not a crash) — indistinguishable from benign crash residue. A persistent legacy-write regression would produce a steadily growing journal-ahead population that the gate waves through forever, and C3's 'zero divergence' claim quietly becomes 'zero divergence of the classes we chose to count'. The classification needs teeth: journal-ahead events OLDER than the bounded tail window (or exceeding a count threshold, or recurring for the same event type across runs) must classify as BUG, and the reconcile-report must surface the journal-ahead census so a trend is visible. Otherwise the gate proves less than the criterion states.

findings.topic: event payload sufficiency for derivation never gated
findings.section: Phase 5 — envelope design vs parity/rebuild deliverables
findings.message: The envelope is 'validated against the three Phase-0 Butler user stories, answerable from envelope fields alone' — but C3's actual proof obligations are different and strictly harder: the parity gate must RE-DERIVE session/effort views from the journal, and rebuild_index.py must reconstruct a deleted index.json. Answering 'what happened on project X this week' requires correlation/actor/ts; rebuilding an index row requires every field the legacy record carries (labels, lanes, chain_id, parent ids, doc rels, statuses, provenance…). The plan validates the schema against the easy consumer and merely asserts the hard consumers will work. There is no payload-completeness gate — no rule that each event type's payload must be sufficient to reconstruct the legacy-store delta it shadows, checked mechanically (e.g. the rebuild test failing on ANY missing field, run per event type, not once against a happy-path fixture). Without it, the schema will be discovered insufficient at rebuild time, forcing either payload-widening churn (schema ver bump per discovery) or a rebuild tool that quietly consults the legacy stores it is supposed to reconstruct.

findings.topic: C2 gate redefined below the criterion
findings.message: C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms 'dispatch through a single declarative table'. The draft's phase gate is explicitly weaker — 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms' — and closure permits the residual to be 'explicitly carried as named debt'. Two problems. First, a route with a declared ROW that still DISPATCHES via the legacy if-elif chain does not satisfy 'dispatch through a single table', and worse, the draft's own strangler wording ('table first, UNMATCHED falls through to the legacy chains') implies an unmigrated route's declared auth policy is never actually EXECUTED on its request path — the row is documentation, not enforcement, for the entire migration tail. Second, the North Star sanctions exactly two narrowings (PTY spike 'no', John declining tokened ops); 'legacy arms carried as named debt' is a third, unsanctioned one smuggled in via the closure phase. Either the plan commits to zero legacy arms within the effort as a C2-blocking gate, or it must route the residual through the amendment path — the scorecard cannot mark C2 met/narrowed on 'named debt'.

findings.topic: Phase-0 contract shim contradicts its own scope and ordering
findings.message: Phase 0 declares 'Nothing here changes runtime behavior' and defers 'any product-behavior change', yet one of its bullets SHIPS a frontend↔backend protocol change: ANCHOR_BOOT carrying a build id, every _postJson sending it, a new structured 409 path, and a reload-required banner. That is product behavior deployed to the live service — a direct internal contradiction with the phase's C7-risk-near-zero framing. It also has an ordering problem: ANCHOR_BOOT is defined in Phase 1 (extraction) as the bootstrap channel the extraction CREATES; in Phase 0 the frontend is still the embedded f-string, so the shim must be retrofitted into the blob that is about to be verbatim-moved — meaning the 'verbatim move' baseline and the Phase-0 census both shift AFTER the census runs. Sequence it honestly: either the shim is a named exception to Phase 0's no-behavior-change rule with its own smoke gate and the census re-run after it lands, or it becomes increment 0 of the extraction phase.

findings.topic: frontend off-switch flag vs shrink gate contradiction
findings.message: The same phase requires the static-vs-embedded off-switch flag to stay 'functional through the phase' AND an exit gate of ≥7,000 lines shrunk. These are mutually exclusive at any single commit: if the embedded f-string path is retained so the flag can flip back, anchor_gui.py has not shrunk; if the blob is deleted to achieve the shrink, the flag's 'embedded' position is dead code-paths pointing at nothing. The overview's blanket claim that 'each merged wave [is] revertible without reverting later waves via per-pillar off-switch flags' is therefore false for this pillar the moment the shrink gate passes — frontend revert becomes git-revert, which later phases touching anchor_gui.py will conflict with. State the actual mechanism per increment: flag-coexistence during the increment's soak, then blob deletion as its own commit, after which revert is git-level and time-bounded.

findings.topic: shrink measurement undefined against thin margin
findings.message: The two cited blobs total ~7,367 lines (4,663 + 2,706) — only ~5% over the 7,000 bar — and the extraction ADDS code to anchor_gui.py (bootstrap-JSON builder, static-root route wiring, build-id minting, cache-bust hashing). If 'shrinks by ≥7,000 lines' is measured as net file-length delta (the natural reading), a few hundred lines of new seam code eat the entire margin and the criterion fails on arithmetic while the work succeeds on substance. The plan should define the measurement now (net wc -l delta of anchor_gui.py, before-vs-after the phase) and let the Phase-0 census confirm the margin, rather than discovering the definition fight at the exit gate.

findings.topic: one-day auth soak misses low-frequency consumers
findings.message: A 'soak day' per route batch on a single-user service exercises John's daily flows and one 5AM healthcheck run, but the consumer inventory the plan itself commissions includes weekly-or-rarer callers: weekly-review habits, occasional .bat/.vbs launcher paths, the iPad PWA over Tailscale (used intermittently), and scheduled tasks that don't fire daily. A warn window that is shorter than the slowest consumer's cadence cannot produce the evidence the gate claims. Either the warn log review must be cross-checked against the Phase-0 consumer inventory as a CHECKLIST (every enumerated consumer observed, or affirmatively exercised by hand) rather than time-boxed, or the soak must span the slowest known cadence for the routes in the batch.

findings.topic: ANCHOR_DATA_DIR propagation to all entry points
findings.message: The migration script sets the env for the NSSM anchor service, but the runtime-state seam is read by MORE entry points: the 'Anchor Health Check' scheduled task (5AM, own environment), 'Anchor Healthcheck.bat', the new supervisor service (Phase 6 clones AppEnvironmentExtra — good, but that's two phases later), and any ad-hoc `python anchor.py rnd …` shell John or a session opens in the repo. Any entry point missing the env silently falls back to the repo-local default and either re-litters the repo (breaking C6's 'stays clean') or, worse, reads a stale split-brain copy of the registry/journal while the service writes the relocated one. The plan needs an explicit propagation checklist (machine-level env var, or every launcher/task rewritten) plus a paths.py-level tripwire that logs/refuses when the resolved data dir is under the repo root post-migration — otherwise 'stays clean through a healthcheck cycle' proves only the one entry point that was scripted.

findings.topic: supervisor-restart probe elevation requirement
findings.message: Probe (b) restarts the SUPERVISOR service nightly/daily from the healthcheck, but service restart on Windows requires elevation and the 5AM healthcheck runs as a non-elevated scheduled task under .\john (the same reason the existing docs say `nssm restart anchor` needs an elevated shell). Either the probe silently degrades to never running (and C4's continuous proof evaporates into the one-time runbook), or the healthcheck task gets elevated rights (a security posture change nobody reviewed), or the supervisor needs a token-authed self-restart IPC verb (new attack surface). The plan should pick one now — this is exactly the kind of 'gate that can't actually run in its scheduled context' the Phase-0 SLO discipline exists to catch, and it's sitting inside the plan's own bullet.

findings.topic: ConPTY spike verdict staleness
findings.message: The ConPTY-across-processes spike runs in Phase 0 but is consumed five phases later, after the extraction, route migration, data-dir move, and journal have all reshaped the codebase (and possibly terminal_session's surroundings). A months-old spike verdict — especially a 'yes' with a latency/complexity budget measured against the pre-refactor code — may no longer describe the system Phase 6 builds on. The plan should either time-bound the verdict's validity (re-affirm the spike's acceptance answers against the then-current code before Phase-6 EXECUTE) or state why the spike's findings are architecture-invariant (pure OS-level ConPTY handle semantics, independent of Anchor's code shape). Cheap to add; prevents building the PTY decision on expired evidence.

findings.topic: 20×-nightly SLO harness is unbuilt infrastructure
findings.message: Both Phase 0 and Phase 7 lean on 'each new walk runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run', but no nightly repetition harness exists today and no phase's near-term specifics builds one — it appears only as a ritual to 'codify'. 20 nightly runs of four new walks is a real scheduled-task + report-aggregation + flake-classification deliverable, and it sits on the critical path of every pillar's healthcheck promotion. Name it as a Phase-0 build item with an owner phase, or the SLO discipline becomes a rule everyone agrees with and nobody can execute.

findings.topic: double phase numbering
findings.message: Every heading carries two colliding indices ('Phase 1 — Phase 0 — Ground Truth…', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — Event-Log Spine'), and the overview's DAG uses yet a third naming (P0/C1/C2…). Foreman waves, gate artifacts, and John's approvals will reference 'Phase 4' and mean two different things. Pick one index before Stage 2 — off-by-one ambiguity in a plan whose whole pitch is mechanical unambiguity.

findings.topic: 52-ideas absorption asserted without traceability artifact
findings.message: The overview claims 'All 52 integrated ideas are absorbed' but the draft ships no traceability table, so the claim is unverifiable by exactly the standard the plan preaches (demonstrated, not narrated). A reviewer cannot confirm from the scattered '(Integrated N)' citations that all of 1–52 appear or that none was silently dropped. Attach the 52-row idea→phase map as a plan appendix. (Process hygiene, not a North-Star criterion — flagged at honest severity.)

reviews.note: Contrarian Shark pass, competitor PM angle: the draft is exhaustive but carries an internal Phase-0 contradiction, one gate that cannot pass as specified, one criterion-narrowing escape hatch, and a daily-use gap that a competing plan would close on day one.

findings.topic: dual phase numbering ambiguity
findings.message: Every phase carries TWO numbers ('Phase 1 — Phase 0', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — Event-Log Spine') and body text cross-references use the inner scheme ('the Phase-3 event envelope' means the header-Phase-5 journal; 'Phase-4 sequencing' means the header-Phase-6 supervisor). Two live numbering schemes in a document that Stage 2 and Foreman will consume mechanically is a misrouting defect, not cosmetics: a wave sequenced against the wrong 'Phase 3' violates the dependency DAG the plan itself declares (journal after data-dir move, supervisor after spike verdict). Collapse to one numbering scheme before Stage 2 or this WILL produce a sequencing error.

findings.topic: Phase 0 self-contradiction — contract shim is a product change that references a not-yet-existing artifact
findings.section: Phase 0 near-term specifics (contract-versioning shim) vs its own deferrals
findings.message: Phase 0's deferral list says 'Any product-behavior change — Phase 0 is instrumentation, spikes, and process artifacts only', yet the same phase ships the frontend↔backend contract shim LIVE ('in the LAST pre-migration release'): new client header on every _postJson, new server 409 path, new banner UI. That is a deployed product-behavior change by any definition. Worse, the shim is specified as 'ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id' — but window.ANCHOR_BOOT is created by the extraction phase that runs AFTER Phase 0; pre-extraction there is no bootstrap JSON for the build id to ride in, so the shim as written depends on an artifact from its own future. Either the shim gets its own pre-extraction injection mechanism (spelled out), or it moves into extraction increment 1 — as drafted the plan's very first deliverable is unimplementable as specified and contradicts its own phase contract.

findings.topic: byte-parity gate infeasible for the interpolated generate_html blob
findings.message: The gate claims OLD-f-string vs NEW-static output is diffed 'byte-for-byte after {{/}} de-escaping', with Playwright reserved for the bootstrap seam. But increment 3 — the generate_html f-string JS/CSS — contains DATA interpolations by construction (the entire reason the Phase-0 census exists). Post-extraction, every data interpolation becomes an ANCHOR_BOOT read or API call, so the static file is NOT byte-equal to the rendered old output precisely in the regions where the risk lives. Byte-parity is only honest for interpolation-free spans. As written, the plan's central C1 gate cannot go green for the one increment it calls 'the only genuinely fiddly one', which means it will be quietly weakened mid-wave — the exact failure mode Phase 0 exists to prevent. Specify the real comparison now: render BOTH paths against one pinned state and compare post-substitution output, or byte-compare only census-classified static spans with the interpolated spans enumerated and Playwright-covered individually.

findings.topic: legacy-arm residual escape hatch narrows C2 without the amendment path
findings.message: C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms 'dispatch through a single declarative table'. Phase 2's gate is explicitly weakened to 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms', and closure then offers 'driven to zero OR its residual explicitly carried as named debt'. 'Named debt' is a narrowing channel that bypasses the North Star's amendment rule — the scorecard clause says any narrowing goes through the documented amendment path, yet this sentence pre-authorizes shipping C2 unmet as mere debt. A competitor plan would be pinned to the criterion: either the zero-arm milestone is a binding exit condition of the effort (state which phase owns it), or the residual case is routed through a John-approved amendment, never a debt register.

findings.topic: every deploy kills live PTYs until the final phase — drain ships too late
findings.section: Phase 0 smoke ritual + Phase 5 drain fallback
findings.message: The per-wave smoke ritual restarts the anchor service at EVERY merged increment across all seven phases, and until the supervisor phase lands, restarts kill in-flight jobs and live PTY sessions — John's actual daily use. The plan pre-DESIGNS the graceful drain (park + capture_session_docs + warm-resume seed) in Phase 0 but only SHIPS it in Phase 5/6 'in the same wave as any narrowing'. That leaves the entire extraction, route, hygiene, and journal campaign — the bulk of the effort's deploys — destroying live context on every merge, which strains 'John's daily use never breaks' for months while the fix sits designed-but-unshipped. Ship the drain script as a Phase-0 deliverable (it composes existing, already-tested primitives: close_session, capture_session_docs, W3 resume) and make it part of the smoke ritual from wave one.

findings.topic: parity gate silently redefines 'zero divergence'
findings.message: C3's bar is 'reports zero divergence'. The gate as designed tolerates a bounded tail window and classifies journal-ahead as OK/crash-residue. Engineering-wise this is defensible, but it is not the locked criterion — it is a redefinition embedded inside a gate implementation. State the delta explicitly (zero divergence AFTER quiescence and journal-ahead reconciliation, with journal-ahead bounded and replayed) and, if that is a narrowing, route it through the amendment path rather than shipping a gate that reports green against a softer bar than the one John locked.

findings.topic: golden corpus of real markdown collides with the no-PII constraint
findings.message: The de-fork gate is 'today's REAL markdown files parsed identically pre/post'. If those files (domains/commercial.md carries proprietary fundraising and relationship detail) are snapshotted into a committed test corpus, the repo's own no-PII/secrets discipline (distro.py scan) is violated and sensitive data gets frozen into git history. Specify now: the golden run executes against the live files in place (uncommitted, environment-local) or against a synthetic corpus that covers every parse construct; a committed real-data corpus is not an option.

findings.topic: one-day auth warn soak under-samples a cron-driven consumer set
findings.message: 'Warn for a soak day' assumes consumers fire daily. This system's callers are cadence-driven: the 5AM healthcheck fires once a day, scheduled tasks and launchers fire irregularly, and the iPad PWA may not be opened for days. A 24-hour warn window can therefore certify a route batch clean while a weekly or occasional consumer is about to be locked out. Bind the soak to coverage, not time: at least one full healthcheck cycle PLUS an affirmative check that every consumer the Phase-0 enumeration listed for those routes appeared in the warn log (or was manually exercised) before enforce.

findings.topic: supervisor IPC auth model unspecified
findings.message: 'Loopback token-authed IPC' is asserted but never specified: same ANCHOR_TOKEN or a distinct supervisor token; whether the supervisor's HTTP surface gets the same default-deny declarative route treatment the effort just built for the dashboard (a second hand-rolled if-elif server would recreate the C2 disease in a new process); and how the token stays in sync across two NSSM services' AppEnvironmentExtra when rotated. install_supervisor.ps1 'clones' the env once — rotation drift between the two services is an unhandled failure row that belongs in the IPC contract table.

findings.topic: 20×-nightly soak has no infrastructure and serializes closure
findings.message: Each of the four new walks must run '20× nightly' before joining the 5AM run, but no nightly-repetition mechanism exists or is planned — that is a new scheduled task (an ops-surface addition the non-goals say this effort doesn't make beyond the supervisor service) and, read literally, ~20 nights of serialized calendar time per walk at the very end of the effort. Define the mechanism now and allow accelerated repetition (20 consecutive runs in one night satisfies the same flake-detection intent) so closure isn't a multi-week idle soak.

findings.topic: data-dir 'rollback' loses interim writes
findings.message: 'Old dir preserved read-only for a week' is a backup, not a rollback plan. Any rollback invoked after real use resumes on the new dir silently discards the sessions, efforts, and (later) journals written there in the interim. Specify the actual rollback procedure — reverse-migrate new-dir deltas back, or an explicit accept-loss statement with the window bounded — so the 'rollback-able unit' claim is honest rather than nominal.

findings.topic: pre-authorized C1 amendment treats John's approval as mechanical
findings.message: The census step says if markup-emitting interpolations exceed a threshold, 'amend the North-Star C1 bar ... NOW'. Amendments require John's decision; the plan phrases this as an automatic consequence of a script's output. Rephrase as a decision gate: census output → present the evidence and the amendment option to John → proceed on his answer. Also state the threshold numerically before the census runs, or the 'small threshold' becomes negotiable after the fact.

findings.topic: no sizing or wave-count estimates
findings.message: A competing plan would carry rough per-phase wave counts and calendar expectations so the seven-phase sequence (with two spikes, a merge freeze, and a 20-night soak) can be sanity-checked against John's tolerance for a months-long substrate effort. No North-Star criterion demands estimates, so this is demoted — but Stage 2 should surface it.

findings.topic: legacy-arm residual escape hatch vs C2 all-routes-through-table
findings.message: C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms route through the single declarative table. The draft quietly redefines the phase gate as 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms', and Phase 7 permits closure with the remaining-legacy-arms counter 'driven to zero OR its residual explicitly carried as named debt'. 'Named debt' is not the documented North-Star amendment path — it is a unilateral criterion dilution pre-authorized inside the plan. A route with a table ROW whose bytes still execute through the legacy if-elif chain has not migrated; the in-branch import-shadowing class C2 also demands dead ('zero remain') survives in every unmigrated arm. Either commit to zero legacy arms as a hard C2 exit condition of the effort, or route the narrowing through the amendment path with John's approval NOW — the plan may not ship its own loophole.

findings.topic: pillar sequencing defers the highest-value pillars to last
findings.message: The bored-investor problem: Stage-0's own oranges framing ranks the event log as the highest-Butler-value pillar and names the supervisor split as the fix for John's REAL recurring pain (nssm restart kills in-flight Foreman runs), yet the plan lands them 5th and 6th of 7 phases, behind frontend extraction, route migration, and repo hygiene. If the effort stalls at 50% — the base case for multi-month re-architectures — John holds a smaller file and identical pain. The dependencies asserted to justify this are thin or fabricated: the journal instruments effort_history/session_registry/terminal_session/job_runner, none of which is blocked by the anchor_gui frontend blobs or the route table; the jobs-half supervisor is called 'low-risk, immediately delivers restart survival' by Stage-0 D2 itself and needs neither the journal (job_runner already has durable records + job-object + creation-time identity) nor 'IPC-adjacent auth' from the route table (loopback token IPC reuses paths.auth_ok directly). Only the data-dir move (journals born outside the repo) is a real ordering constraint. Re-sequence so at least one of C3/C4 (recommend the jobs-half supervisor) lands in the first half of the effort, or state honestly why value is being deferred.

findings.topic: Phase 0 packs planning work whose output can invalidate the locked plan
findings.message: Phase 0 defers to build-time ground truth that is cheap, mechanical, and knowable during planning — and whose answer gates the plan's own validity. The interpolation census in particular decides whether the C1 bar (≥7,000-line shrink, ~50-line blob cap) must be amended 'NOW, not mid-wave' — meaning the plan is being locked while explicitly anticipating an immediate amendment to its first success criterion. A grep-classifiable census over two known line ranges, the consumer-enumeration grep, the dependency DAG, and the three Butler user stories are all Stage-1/Stage-2 planning artifacts; running them DURING Stage 2 (before Foreman) resolves the C1 bar, the open-route consumer set, and the event-envelope validation target before anything is committed. As drafted, Phase 0 is ~12 deliverables spanning two spikes, a Playwright suite, a tripwire harness, a deploy shim, process rituals, and a freeze protocol — a whole sub-project labeled 'instrumentation' with no sizing, delaying all user-visible value behind it. Pull the paper artifacts into Stage 2; keep Phase 0 to the two spikes, the Playwright flows, and the tripwire.

findings.topic: journal emit() failure semantics unspecified under journal-first ordering
findings.message: The plan decrees emit-event-THEN-write-legacy at every mutation-of-record, but never specifies what happens when emit() itself FAILS (disk full, schema-validation bug, lock contention, a malformed payload from one of ~10 instrumented subsystems). If emit() raising blocks the legacy write, a journal bug takes down the authoritative store path across session lifecycle, jobs, grass, and deliverables simultaneously — inverting D1 ('legacy stores stay authoritative') and violating C7, with the blast radius of the one choke point the design celebrates. The off-switch flag is a human-latency remedy, not a failure semantic. The plan must state the rule: emit() is fail-open with respect to the legacy write (log + counter + healthcheck surface on journal-write failure; legacy write ALWAYS proceeds), and the parity gate's classification must include 'legacy-ahead-because-emit-failed' as distinguishable from the BUG class.

findings.topic: no sizing, duration, or wave-count estimates anywhere in the plan
findings.message: Seven phases, roughly sixty near-term specifics, two spikes, four new healthcheck walks, a second NSSM service — and not one phase carries a size, wave count, or rough duration. The investor cannot judge whether the Phase-0 front-load pays back, whether the extraction merge-freeze window is days or weeks (it must be coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build, which needs a real window, not 'a soft freeze'), or whether the plan fits any horizon at all. C7's no-multi-day-freeze and never-broken-increment clauses are unverifiable without at least coarse per-phase sizing and an explicit statement of what gets CUT first if the effort must shrink. A FULL-pipeline Stage-1 master plan should rank the phases by value-per-cost and mark the minimum shippable subset (per the North Star: jobs-half C4 is non-negotiable; C1's bar is amendable) — this draft treats all seven phases as equally mandatory and unpriced.

findings.topic: Phase-0 'no runtime change' claim contradicted by the contract shim, which also references a not-yet-existing ANCHOR_BOOT
findings.message: Phase 0's framing paragraph claims 'Nothing here changes runtime behavior, so C7 risk is near zero', yet one of its own deliverables ships a frontend↔backend contract shim to the LIVE service: ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, the server 409s a mismatch. That is a client+server behavior change with its own stale-tab failure modes — exactly the class it exists to prevent. Worse, window.ANCHOR_BOOT does not exist until the Phase-1 extraction introduces the bootstrap JSON; in Phase 0 the build id must ride the still-embedded f-string, meaning the shim is built twice or the plan's dependency arrow is backwards. State honestly that Phase 0 contains one behavior-bearing deploy, and specify the pre-extraction carrier for the build id.

findings.topic: tripwire enumeration mode vs permanent enforcement mode conflated
findings.section: Phase 1 (Phase 0) write-site tripwire / Phase 5 completeness gate
findings.message: Phase 0 says the tripwire 'fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event' and 'stays on forever' — but no journal exists until Phase 5, so between Phase 0 and Phase 5 the tripwire in failing mode would redden the entire suite. It plainly needs two modes (enumerate/report in Phases 0–4, enforce from Phase 5), yet the plan never says so, nor who owns the allowlist of legitimately-unjournaled writes (per-tick/telemetry 'excluded BY RULE' — which rule, checked where?) as the codebase drifts between the two phases. Specify the mode switch, its flip point, and the allowlist's review discipline, or the C3 completeness gate is a gate only in narrative.

findings.topic: parity-gate tail tolerance vs C3's 'zero divergence'
findings.message: C3 requires the parity gate to report ZERO divergence; the draft's gate 'tolerates a bounded tail window of recent events' and classifies journal-ahead as OK. Reasonable engineering for a live 5AM run, but as written it is a weaker predicate than the criterion. Make the two-tier structure explicit: the TEST-suite parity gate runs quiescent and asserts literal zero divergence (the C3 bar), while the live healthcheck run applies the bounded-tail classification with journal-ahead-within-window as the only tolerated class — and any legacy-ahead or conflict is a hard failure in both tiers. Otherwise the scorecard will mark C3 'met' against a diluted definition.

findings.topic: '20× nightly' soak infrastructure does not exist and is unowned
findings.message: The plan repeatedly invokes a rule that each new healthcheck walk 'runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run', but the host has exactly one scheduled run (5AM) — there is no nightly-repetition harness, no scheduled task for it, and no phase deliverable that builds one. Four new walks (journal parity, supervisor probes, cookie/auth, relocated-data-dir) are gated on this nonexistent infrastructure. Either name the harness as a Phase-0/Phase-6 deliverable (a second scheduled task + a repetition report) or replace the rule with something the current infrastructure can enforce.

findings.topic: double phase numbering
findings.message: Every section is double-numbered ('Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — …'), so the ConPTY-spike directive ('early'), cross-references like 'Phase-3 event envelope' (which is Phase 5's content under the outer numbering), and any Foreman wave mapping are ambiguous by one everywhere. Pick one numbering before Stage 2 or the implementation plan will inherit off-by-one references.

findings.topic: unverifiable 'all 52 integrated ideas absorbed' claim
findings.message: The preamble asserts 'All 52 integrated ideas are absorbed' and specifics cite opaque tags (Integrated 1..52, Mitigation 1..20) that appear nowhere in the North Star or the visible research input, so neither the Sharks nor the Judge can verify absorption or spot a silently dropped idea. Attach the numbered idea/mitigation ledger as a plan appendix or drop the claim.
